Most hotels in Yemen are like this. You search and find pictures of living rooms, but no pictures of bedrooms, no prices, and no information about available services. The room rates are good.

They have Starlink internet, which I really liked, and they offer internet speed options from 512 kbps to 4 Gbps.

The electricity does cut out when the generator is running, but the important thing is that it's continuous.

Their services are good. If you need them to pick up groceries, take your laundry, or order lunch, they'll deliver, but not from far away.
The reception staff are excellent and straightforward, and you have a landline to call them. However, once another employee answered the phone and was rude, not letting me finish my sentence and hanging up without bringing what I requested.

A mattress and pillow are provided.

Negatives:
The biggest problem I faced was the lack of room maintenance. Sometimes I found a broken plug, other times the shower leaked excessively, and the sink drain had a problem. I moved to another room where everything was fine. I was given a room where the bathroom was very small. You could barely shower and couldn't be careful not to bump your head or fall into the drain (excuse the expression). I moved to another room which was much better.

The towel in the room was very old. I wasn't happy with the laundry; there were still stains and dust residue. However, the ironing was excellent.

My overall rating is 4 stars. I recommend checking the bathroom before booking a room. The hotel needs to pay more attention to maintenance and the quality of the laundry. Adding insult to injury, the decision to cover the bed mattresses with leather was nothing short of a nightmare, the leather covering not only made the beds uncomfortably hot but also disrupted my sleep further, It seemed like a deliberate ploy to compel guests to opt for the additional AC package, extracting more money from their wallets.

This meant that if I wanted to go anywhere, even just to the first floor, I had to take the NFC card with me. As a result, the moment the NFC card left the rented room, the electricity would be abruptly cut off within ten seconds. This cumbersome process not only made it inconvenient for guests but also created unnecessary complications, especially when traveling with a partner.

All in all, my stay at the Mariot Taiz Hotel was far from satisfactory. The high prices, cramped rooms, additional charges for basic amenities, lackluster bathrooms, and hassle of using the elevator system profoundly affected my overall experience negatively. The Good:
The hotel is very quiet and convenient for travelers, situated in a location that made getting around easy. The rooms are impressively spacious, providing plenty of room to spread out, and are equipped with the bare necessities—exactly what we needed for a simple base. The peaceful atmosphere was a highlight, allowing for good rest. For the price point, the value was okay and met our basic expectations for a short trip.

The Not-So-Good:
Unfortunately, the maintenance and service left a bit to be desired and disrupted our stay.

Maintenance: We dealt with a leaking sink in the kitchen that was constant and annoying. Additionally, our keycards stopped working multiple times throughout the stay. It was quite a hassle to repeatedly walk back to the front desk to get them reset just to enter our room.

Service: The breakfast service was unreliable. On our second day, breakfast was never delivered at all. We called to follow up and waited over 45 minutes hoping it would arrive, but it never did, which delayed our morning plans.

Verdict:
If you are looking for a spacious and quiet place to sleep without breaking the bank, this works well.
